# Teaching a New Colleague: Passing On Practical Skills in the Workshop

When a new colleague joins a workshop, the first weeks determine whether they become a confident, capable member of the team or a hesitant worker who constantly second-guesses themselves. Teaching a practical job is not simply a matter of showing someone what to do and expecting them to copy it. It requires structure, patience, and an honest understanding of what matters and what does not. Over years of training new machinists, fitters, and fabricators, I have settled on a method that works reliably: demonstrate one complete task from start to finish, explain the decisions behind each step while I work, hand the task over to the learner, resist the urge to correct every small difference, separate safety-critical steps from personal habits, leave behind usable notes, and finally check understanding with a fresh example. Each element matters, and together they form a complete approach to passing on practical knowledge.

## Start with One Complete Task
